definition: Integral Channel Features (ICF), also known as ChnFtrs, is a method for object detection in computer vision.
details: It uses integral images to extract features such as local sums, histograms and Haar-like features from multiple registered image channels. This method was highly exploited by Dollár et al. in their work for pedestrian detection, that was first described at the BMVC in 2009.

explainer.lead: Integral Channel Features (ICF), also known as ChnFtrs, is a method for object detection in computer vision. It was heavily exploited by Dollár et al. for pedestrian detection, first described at BMVC in 2009.

tiers.eli5: It scans a picture in several filtered versions at once and adds up small regions quickly to spot objects like people.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use integral images to extract features such as local sums, histograms, and Haar-like features from multiple registered image channels. A pitfall is that features depend on the channels being registered to one another.
tiers.paperLevel: A method for object detection in computer vision that uses integral images to extract features such as local sums, histograms, and Haar-like features from multiple registered image channels. First described at BMVC in 2009 in work on pedestrian detection.

explainer.example: In pedestrian detection, ICF computes local sums and Haar-like features over registered channels using integral images to locate people in an image.
